new_findings.subject: Colegio de San Ignacio secular exemption
new_findings.assertion: 6 January 1861 order exempted Colegio de Niñas de San Ignacio from nationalization; dissolved Cofradía de Aránzazu's patronage passed to civic board headed by Ignacio Jaynaga.

new_findings.subject: Pre-decree civilian inspection
new_findings.assertion: Before February law, Juárez commissioned Luis Garrone and Juan Navarro to inspect Divino Salvador and San Hipólito hospitals' condition and funds.
new_findings.locator: printed p.60 note 137, citing La Reforma 26 Jan 1861 t.I no.26 f.2

new_findings.subject: Directorate creation and institutional jurisdiction
new_findings.assertion: Dirección General de Beneficencia Pública founded 28 February 1861; disputes with Ayuntamiento over Tecpam de Santiago, Hospicio de Pobres, Casa de Corrección, Niños Expósitos.

new_findings.subject: Administering welfare categories
new_findings.assertion: 1861 Directorate regulations assigned child vaccination, foundling care, institutional assistance, and work for beggars; semiannual staff meetings and budget oversight were prescribed.

new_findings.subject: Municipal objection
new_findings.assertion: 12 April 1861 Ayuntamiento protested federal takeover of charitable powers and retained spending obligations; urged abolition of federal Directorate arrangement.

new_findings.subject: Contested cost sharing
new_findings.assertion: December 1861 compromise assigned care contributions to both Directorate and city council; April 1862 complaints said central salaries diverted money needed by Hospital San Pablo.

new_findings.subject: Abolition of central Directorate
new_findings.assertion: Government abolished Dirección General de Beneficencia Pública on 30 Aug 1862; notice returned welfare institutions to district municipalities amid fiscal and war pressures.

new_findings.subject: Imperial municipality projected shortfall
new_findings.assertion: Jan 1865 capital budget projected 1,171,767.45 pesos in costs versus 683,086 income; planned 73,784 for San Andrés; 39,120 San Pablo; 71,992 Hospicio de Pobres; other named hospitals.

new_findings.subject: Carlota and welfare credit
new_findings.assertion: Sept 1865 Consejo General de Beneficencia chaired by Carlota announced government approval of 20,000-peso credit for institutions, to allocate by needs.

new_findings.subject: San Andrés transformed into hospital
new_findings.assertion: After Jesuit expulsion, an epidemic prompted bishop’s request for 400-bed hospital at San Andrés site in 1769; in 1783 government turned it over for archiepiscopal management.

new_findings.subject: 1867 imperial memory reshaped street
new_findings.assertion: San Andrés held Maximilian's body for embalming in 1867; former chapel was destroyed in 1868 and Xicoténcatl street cut through, in historian's account.

new_findings.subject: From hospital to communications palace
new_findings.assertion: 1904 San Andrés demolition on Tacuba; Contri Communications Palace started 1905 with named foreign contractors; occupied under Madero 1912; MUNAL opened 1982.
new_findings.locator: sections La demolición and El palacio

new_findings.subject: Hospital de Jesús institutional exception
new_findings.assertion: Official CDMX heritage guide attributes survival of Hospital de Jesús amid Reform to secular foundation; León Garduño lists Hospital de Jesús among privately administered 1861 establishments.
new_findings.locator: section ¿En operación desde 1524?; León Garduño p.60 n.138
